classification.difficultyReason: Find and mark the intercepts of a restricted cosine curve, then use those intercepts as exact integration limits.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Sketch the curve $y=2\cos\pi x$, for $-1\leq x\leq1$, clearly marking the two $x$-intercepts.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}2\cos\pi x&=0\\\cos\pi x&=0\\x&=-\frac12,\ \frac12\end{align*}$$
The curve is symmetric about the $y$-axis, has maximum $(0,2)$ and includes the endpoints $(-1,-2)$ and $(1,-2)$.

spec.description: Complete restricted cosine sketch with labelled intercepts, positive central maximum, closed negative endpoints and double-ended coordinate axes. Teacher-answer blue is rendered in ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: y=2 cos(pi x) on [-1,1], with intercepts (-1/2,0) and (1/2,0), maximum (0,2) and endpoints (-1,-2),(1,-2).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the exact area bounded by the curve $y=2\cos\pi x$ and the $x$-axis, between the two $x$-intercepts.
